profile.name: Tobi Awolaju
profile.title: Engineer · Builder · Researcher
profile.bio:
I build across software, blockchain, AI, and physical systems. From real-time multiplayer infrastructure and autonomous agents to experimental electronics and telecommunications research, I turn difficult problems into working systems.

Final-year Electrical Engineering student at Adeleke University, Nigeria · Independent builder
Open to junior engineering roles, remote opportunities, internships, and applied R&D.

projects.title: World of Nads ↗
projects.description: Browser-based 3D multiplayer arena game. Godot client compiled to WebAssembly for zero-install delivery, 20Hz authoritative Rust WebSocket multiplayer server synchronizing players in real time, and Monad EVM smart contracts for prize distribution.

writeup.hardPart: Keeping player state synchronized over WebSockets in real time while the browser also handles a wallet layer and on-chain state without frame collapses. I profiled and resolved a critical bottleneck where per-frame function calls crossing the Godot-WASM to JavaScript DOM bridge tanked browser frame rates from 60 FPS to under 12 FPS on lower-end devices; rebuilt the sync path around batched 20Hz delta frames and contiguous typed arrays.
highlights: Real-time 20Hz authoritative Rust WebSocket state synchronization server
Zero-install 3D arena client delivered via Godot WebAssembly (WASM) & WebGL
Optimistic client-side movement interpolation with server reconciliation
Decoupled render loops from network dispatch to eliminate V8 GC stalls
Monad EVM smart contracts for escrow match entry and on-chain prize payouts
Custom compact framing reducing WebSocket wire serialization payload
writeup.stack: Godot (WASM), Rust (Tokio WebSocket Server), TypeScript, Solidity (Monad EVM), PostgreSQL, Privy Auth.

projects.title: EEG Communication Headset ↗
projects.description: Experimental hardware and firmware investigation exploring an affordable, wearable communication-support interface for non-speaking users. Integrates scalp dry electrodes, a NeuroSky TGAM biosensing frontend, an ESP32 microcontroller, audio amplification, and bone-conduction transducers.

writeup.hardPart: Physiological signals acquired at the scalp are in the microvolt range (10-100 μV) and easily corrupted by ocular blinks, jaw clenches (EMG), and 50Hz mains hum. Isolating deliberate, intentional user triggers on a low-power microcontroller without false positives required strict FreeRTOS task isolation across ESP32 cores and a custom ThinkGear UART packet parser.
highlights: Benchtop test bench established with TGAM biosensing module and ESP32-WROOM-32
Dual-core FreeRTOS firmware: Core 0 parses 57,600 baud serial packets; Core 1 runs event state machines
ThinkGear UART packet parser with strict 0xAA 0xAA sync byte and checksum verification
PAM8403 audio amplifier stage driving 8Ω bone-conduction transducers against temporal bones
Honest scope: Designed as a discrete intentional trigger interface (not arbitrary sentence/thought decoding)
Hardware assembled and bench-tested; custom PCB layout and ergonomic 3D-printed headband in progress
writeup.stack: ESP32 (FreeRTOS / C++), NeuroSky TGAM ASIC, UART Serial Protocol, PAM8403 Audio Amp, Bone Conduction Transducers.

projects.title: Cellular Fingerprint Positioning System ↗
projects.description: Final-year Electrical Engineering capstone project at Adeleke University. Investigating position estimation algorithms in urban and indoor environments using cellular signal fingerprints (GSM/LTE RSSI, Cell ID, LAC) where satellite GPS signals are severely attenuated or unavailable.

writeup.hardPart: Cellular Received Signal Strength Indicator (RSSI) exhibits high temporal and spatial variance caused by shadow fading, structural multipath, and dynamic network load balancing, rendering naive geometric trilateration error-prone indoors.
highlights: Final-year Electrical Engineering capstone research project at Adeleke University
Hardware survey test rig logging cellular modem registers (AT+CSQ, AT+CREG, AT+COPS) with timestamped coordinates
Multi-cell fingerprint vector construction combining serving cell and neighbor cell signal levels
Offline radio map calibration linked with online k-Nearest Neighbors (k-NN) and probabilistic matching
Ongoing empirical grid survey across campus outdoor-to-indoor transition zones
Constructing baseline error Cumulative Distribution Function (CDF) curves for thesis evaluation
writeup.stack: Cellular Telephony (GSM/LTE), AT-Command Modems, Python (NumPy / SciPy), k-NN Classification, RF Propagation Modeling.

projects.title: KYP ↗
projects.description: On-chain protocol accountability platform. Research protocols with an AI pipeline, commit with a wallet stake, and let smart contracts automatically verify your follow-through across EVM protocols without custom event signatures.

writeup.hardPart: Building a protocol-agnostic verification system that works across any EVM protocol without relying on custom event signatures or proprietary ABI decoders. Designed an architecture that scans user on-chain activity using indexed getLogs queries, filters engagement by protocol contract, and automatically resolves commitments through Solidity vaults and a heartbeat-driven backend worker.
highlights: Dual-tier AI research pipeline (FlashResearcher + DeepResearcher via Gemini)
Protocol-agnostic engagement detection across arbitrary EVM smart contracts using getLogs
Solidity commitment contracts with automatic 9-day, 3-strike verify/slash execution
Zero-cost heartbeat worker architecture avoiding expensive third-party cron services
Multi-network support (Monad Testnet + Mainnet) with adaptive block-time estimation
Recognized during the BuildAnything Spark Hackathon with 100% verified test harness
writeup.stack: Svelte 5, TypeScript, Node.js, Solidity, viem, ethers, Firebase RTDB, Gemini API, Privy, Monad.

projects.title: Rug Pool ↗
projects.description: Memecoin launchpad where no one — not even the deployer — can exit early. On-chain, verifiable randomness decides who exits at the 24-hour mark; losers fund the winner's payout.

writeup.hardPart: Enforcing a hard lock at the contract level with no admin backdoor, while making the randomness both unpredictable and independently verifiable. Used Pyth Entropy for VRF. Shipped 5 contracts to Monad testnet with 53 passing tests and ran two full simulation cycles to confirm the payout logic held under edge cases.
highlights: Non-custodial contract exit constraints enforced at the EVM bytecode level
Pyth Entropy VRF integration for verifiable tamper-proof randomness
53 automated passing unit and integration tests on Hardhat
writeup.stack: Solidity, Hardhat, Monad, Pyth VRF, TypeScript, React.
